judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not mention emcee being described as a 'nested sampling code' or challenge the characterization of emcee against the Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 citation. The reviewer mentions SED fitting with prospector but never flags the MCMC/nested sampling categorization of emcee.

The review mentions SED fitting with prospector in the summary but does not flag the statement that emcee is a nested sampling code or challenge the Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 citation/method categorization.
The reviewer mentions the use of Prospector for SED fitting but does not mention emcee or the incorrect categorization of it as a nested sampling code.

The reviewer does not flag the characterization of emcee as a 'nested sampling code' anywhere in the report. The review does not challenge the method category assigned to emcee or contrast it with the Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 paper, which describes emcee as an MCMC ensemble sampler.

The reviewer does not flag any inconsistency between the abstract redshift z=3.17 and the body's z=3.71 for the Jekyll & Hyde overdensity. The reviewer's summary correctly states z=3.71 in the paper summary, but never explicitly flags the discrepancy as an error to be corrected.

Although the reviewer summary correctly states z = 3.71, they do not explicitly flag an inconsistency in the abstract or identify the erroneous z=3.17 value, so this does not count as a specific detection.
The reviewer uses the correct redshift (z=3.71) in their summary, indicating they read the value from the body of the paper and failed to notice the typo (z=3.17) in the abstract.

The reviewer consistently and correctly refers to the Jekyll & Hyde system as being at z=3.71 throughout the report (e.g., 'two high-redshift overdense regions at z = 3.71'), and never flags the abstract's erroneous z=3.17. The injected discrepancy between the abstract (z=3.17) and body (z=3.71) was not caught.

The reviewer does not mention any issue with the overdensity equation (Eq. 1) or the sign in the numerator of the delta definition. No mathematical error in the formula is flagged anywhere in the report.
The reviewer discusses the overdensity scale and cites delta values, but never flags Eq. 1 or the overdensity definition as algebraically incorrect.
The reviewer discusses the overdensity estimation methods and smoothing scales in Section 2.2 but makes no mention of the erroneous sign in the definition of delta in Equation 1.

The reviewer discusses the overdensity estimation methodology and smoothing scale in Major Comment 3, but never flags an error in Equation 1 itself. No reviewer comment identifies the sign error (+ instead of −) in the numerator of the overdensity definition δ = (n+n̄)/n̄.
The reviewer does not flag any cross-reference mismatch between fig:densz4 and the COSMOS field description. No comment about an incorrect figure reference in Sec. 2.1 is present in the report.
There is no comment about a mismatched figure reference for the COSMOS overdensity sentence or any cross-reference problem between fig:dens and fig:densz4.
The reviewer mentions the overdensity values for both the COSMOS and SXDS fields but does not flag the mismatch between the text description and the figure cross-reference.

The reviewer does not flag any mismatch between a figure cross-reference and its described content. No comment is made about Figure 2 being referenced where Figure 1 is described, or any COSMOS/SXDS figure label confusion.
